maya: Quick heads-up — P95 on /v1/generate-chat jumped ~40ms after yesterday's prefetch tweak. Noticed a KV miss rate spike for routes in the enterprise tier.

oliver: Ugh. Is it correlated with any kernel handoff points?

maya: Yeah, profiler shows an extra kernel selection event when sequence length crosses 32 tokens. It forces a microbatch split and we lose batching efficiency.

kevin: Do we have the trace for a single request? Can you paste the slice where kernel switch happens?

maya: Pasted a trimmed trace below (from the canary run):
```
[trace] route: /v1/generate-chat enterprise
tokens: 36
kernel_select: base_kernel -> kv_prefetch_kernel (at token 32)
microbatch_split: 1 -> 2
kv_miss: 0.27 -> 0.62
latency_p95: 162ms -> 203ms
```

sara: Hmm. Looks like the prefetch window isn't covering the tail tokens. Our KV prefetch threshold was 32 to avoid early prefetch costs, but that means some longer prompts force a kernel switch.

oliver: Could we make the prefetch heuristic SLO-driven? e.g., for enterprise tier, if p95 target is 120ms, allow prefetch up to 48 tokens to avoid kernel swaps.

kevin: I tried a local experiment bumping route token_budget for enterprise to 96 and the p95 dropped 30ms, but cost increased ~7%. Tradeoff seems acceptable for that tier.

maya: Can you drop the exact commands you used to run the canary? I'll reproduce.

kevin: Sure — ran a canary with this config:
```json
{
  "route": "/v1/generate-chat",
  "tier": "enterprise",
  "token_budget": 96,
  "prefetch_threshold": 48,
  "queue_policy": "slo_led"
}
```
Command: `./infra/canary/run_canary --config canary-enterprise.json --duration 10m`

perf-bot: Canary run summary (canary-enterprise.json): p95: 133ms -> 103ms; cost/op +7.1%; KV hit rate +12.4%; kernel_switches -72%.

sara: Nice. That aligns with hypothesis. We should roll a targeted experiment: SLO-led prefetch for enterprise routes only, with fallback to default for lower tiers. Keep canary narrow.

oliver: Also want to test queue policy impact. Our FIFO queue holds batches longer when prefetched; slo_led queue will prioritize early completion routes but might starve background batch packing. Need a short AB test comparing "slo_led" vs "throughput_opt".

maya: Agreed — propose rollout plan: 1) run 30m AB canary (enterprise routes) comparing token_budget 64 vs 96 with slo_led queue; 2) measure p95, KV hit, cost/op; 3) if p95 reduces >=20ms and cost <12% bump, promote.

kevin: I'll provision canary, add a kernel switch counter and microbatch split metric to the dashboard. Also will add a tiny regression guard: if kernel_switches drop but tail-latency increases for small requests, abort.

oliver: One more note — update kernel selector to consider route tier when deciding prefetch kernel. Right now it's stateless (just seq len); adding tier should avoid cross-route regressions.

maya: I'll file a small follow-up PR to kernel_selector: add route_tier bias and expose token_budget override from route config.

perf-bot: Created ticket RN-1142 "slo-led prefetch experiment for enterprise routes" and scheduled canary at 22:15 UTC.

sara: Thanks team. I'll monitor dashboards and post final numbers to #eng-runtime when canary ends. :thumbsup:

maya: TY — let's sync after the canary. :coffee:
